channel.title: Journal on Stephanie Tess van Slyck
channel.description: Recent content in Journal on Stephanie Tess van Slyck

item.title: Where MCP Would Fit in a Project Like Standflow
item.description: Model Context Protocol is not a replacement for a REST API. A short reflection on what it is, and where it would actually belong in a system I have already built.

item.title: The Excursion I Missed, and Building for a Place I Had Not Seen
item.description: The class visited the customer site. I could not attend, so this is about building for a context I only knew second-hand, and where the project stands.

item.title: Secrets, Escaping and Safe Choices
item.description: How keys, escaping and consent are handled across my two projects, and why the safest choices were the ones that removed the unsafe option rather than guarding it.

item.title: Building a Whole Project with a Code Agent
item.description: I used an AI code agent to take over and finish an entire group project, Standflow. This is the honest version: what the agent did, what I kept for myself, the guardrails that made it safe, the near-disaster, and what actually makes agentic development work.

item.title: Standflow: From a Manor-House Visit to a Working System
item.description: The project case: a real customer with a real problem, the idea we proposed, and the system we sketched and then built to solve it.

item.title: Architecture of an LLM-Backed Rubric Assessor
item.description: How a small Express service turns a rubric and a student report into structured, schema-validated AI feedback: the data flow, the prompt contract, the error handling, and how it was tested without a real API call.

item.title: Building an AI Rubric Assessor: What Today Actually Taught Me
item.description: A personal walkthrough of building a small AI grading tool: the loose thoughts I started with, the wall I hit, and what it taught me about trusting a model to judge someone else’s work.
